related_questions.question: How to not catch COVID from someone in your house?

text_blocks.snippet: To avoid catching COVID-19 from someone in your household, the most effective strategies involve minimizing contact and improving ventilation. This includes isolating the infected person, using masks, and improving airflow.

list.title: Isolate the infected person:
list.snippet: If possible, designate a separate room and bathroom for the individual with COVID-19.

list.title: Mask up:
list.snippet: When contact is unavoidable, both the infected person and those interacting with them should wear well-fitting masks (surgical or KN95 recommended).

list.title: Improve ventilation:
list.snippet: Open windows and use fans to increase airflow and reduce viral concentration in shared spaces, according to the CDC.

list.title: Hand hygiene:
list.snippet: Frequent handwashing with soap and water or using hand sanitizer is crucial.

list.title: Clean frequently touched surfaces:
list.snippet: Regularly disinfect surfaces like doorknobs, light switches, and countertops.

list.title: Consider air purifiers:
list.snippet: If available, using air purifiers with HEPA filters can help remove viral particles from the air.

list.title: Monitor symptoms:
list.snippet: Watch for any signs of illness and get tested if symptoms develop.

related_questions.question: What is the best thing to do if you have COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, the best course of action is to isolate at home to prevent further spread, and monitor your symptoms closely. If you are at higher risk for severe illness or experiencing severe symptoms, consult your doctor promptly, as they may recommend specific treatments.
snippet_highlighted_words: isolate at home to prevent further spread, and monitor your symptoms closely

list.snippet: Stay home to prevent the spread of the virus.
Inform close contacts about your positive test result.
Watch for any worsening symptoms, particularly those listed as emergency warning signs (such as difficulty breathing, persistent pain or pressure in the chest, etc.).
Seek immediate medical attention for any severe symptoms.
Get plenty of rest to allow your body to recover.
Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of fluids.
Over-the-counter medications like pain relievers and fever reducers can help manage symptoms.
Consult your doctor about any specific treatments that may be beneficial.
If you are at higher risk of severe illness, your doctor may recommend treatments like antiviral medications to reduce the risk of hospitalization.
Engage in activities you enjoy, like listening to music or reading, to help pass the time and manage stress.
Stay connected with loved ones through phone or video calls.

text_blocks.snippet: By following these steps, you can effectively manage your COVID-19 infection, prevent its spread, and prioritize your recovery.
